incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency SLO breached for customer Corvid (hosted, single-tenant). Trigger: streaming stalls + elevated p99 > 2s for last 5m. Paging on-call now. :rotating_light:
Ravi Patel: I'm on it. grabbing traces + current p95/p99 numbers.
Alice Chen: I can help with routing rules and KV cache checks. tagging @Corvid-SRE for context.
Corvid-SRE: saw a jump in concurrent streaming sessions ~16:10 UTC, some sessions reporting repeated stall frames. Customers report partial responses + long time-to-first-byte.
Ravi Patel: quick metrics snapshot: p95=480ms, p99=2.6s, streaming stall count increased from 2/min to 34/min. Error budget burn ~7% over 10m.
Kenji Sato: putting up trace sample: `trace_id=trc-0x9fc3` shows spikes at token generation step: heavy kvcache misses + retry backoff in runtime.
Alice Chen: suspecting unusual prompt fanout: Corvid recently rolled a campaign that concatenates long multi-turn prefixes + many short followups. This spikes prefix KV utilization.
María Gómez: any quick mitigations? customers getting UX regressions. Corvid-SRE says they can tolerate brief model fallback to lower-latency variant.
Ravi Patel: immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable tenant routing to fallback model variant rwd-small-latency for stream sessions 2) bypass prefix KV caching for tenant for 10m 3) temporarily scale dedicated pool by +1 replica. Applying 1 & 2 now.
Alice Chen: command to enable routing change: ```
rb routes update --tenant=corvid --route=streaming --model=rwd-small-latency --sticky=false
```
Alice Chen: command to bypass KV cache: ```
rb tenant-config set corvid runtime.kvcache.enabled=false --dur=10m
```
Laura Mills: scaling dedicated pool: ```
rb scale pool corvid-dedicated --replicas +1 --reason "incident 1799998888"
```
incident-bot: NOTE: change requests logged (change-id: chg-20260315-1799).
Ravi Patel: rolled routing to fallback and KV bypass applied. scaling request triggered. Observability: p99 trending down.
Corvid-SRE: confirming on their side: initial monitors show stream stalls dropping immediately. They see sessions resume normal TTFB within ~30s.
Kenji Sato: grabbing flamegraph/snippet from runtime logs: ```
[2026-03-15T16:12:05Z] model_gen.ms=120 kvcache.lookup.ms=38 kvcache.miss=true kv_eviction_count=12
[2026-03-15T16:12:07Z] retry.backoff.ms=250 stall_frame.count=3
```
Ravi Patel: good sign. p99 now ~820ms at 16:13 UTC. p95 ~420ms. Stall rate down to 4/min.
Alice Chen: root-cause hypothesis: Corvid campaign created many long shared prefixes across very high concurrency sessions; KV cache thrash + evictions introduced backpressure to the runtime's streaming path, causing stalls in the last-token emission (tail latency).
María Gómez: customer impact estimate: roughly 12% of Corvid requests experienced >1s tail stalls during peak window (16:05-16:15 UTC). Corvid reports increased abandonment for a subset of live users.
Corvid-SRE: confirming impact on a handful of premium tenants; they'd like post-incident report + remediation checklist.
Ravi Patel: follow-ups while oncall: 1) capture golden replay of correlated requests (we'll ask Corvid to share sanitized prompt samples) 2) run local reproducer with the runtime toggles to validate KV behavior 3) instrument more granular prefix eviction counters per-tenant 4) evaluate short-term auto-increase of kvcache size for single-tenant pools.
Alice Chen: creating a temporary alert rule to detect kvcache_evictions/spike for single-tenant pools: ```
alert kvcache_eviction_spike if sum(kvcache.evictions{tenant=~"corvid.*"}) by (tenant) > 5 for 1m
```
Kenji Sato: logging note: captured traces and a trace-sample bundle at s3://redwood-incident-bundles/1799998888/traces.tar.gz (permission: eng-sre + corvid-sre).
Laura Mills: scaling success: corvid-dedicated scaled +1 -> replicas now 3. autoscaler stable.
Ravi Patel: mitigation verified, moving to recovery phase. Rolling back temporary KV bypass in 30m once caches warmed and model fallback performance validated.
Corvid-SRE: appreciate the quick action. we'll also patch client to reduce prefix fanout for next campaign.
María Gómez: impact notify draft: "We observed elevated tail latency for streaming responses affecting ~12% of requests during a 10-minute window; we mitigated by routing to a lower-latency model and scaling capacity. We're investigating root cause and will share a detailed postmortem." Thoughts?
Ravi Patel: fine to send; include that we collected sanitized prompts and plan kvcache instrumentation.
Alice Chen: adding follow-up action items (post-incident): 1) permanent routing rule for fallback under kvcache_eviction_spike 2) per-tenant kvcache capacity knob + autoscale policy 3) eval model quantization profile to reduce token-gen variance 4) run blue-green test for Corvid campaign before wide rollout.
Corvid-SRE: we'll provide prompt samples and traffic patterns by EOD. request: please include a small pre-warm API we can call to warm the cache before big campaigns.
Ravi Patel: noted; will coordinate on pre-warm API (owner: Alice).
incident-bot: INCIDENT update: status=mitigated, mitigation_time=16:14:22 UTC, owner=Ravi Patel. retention bundle uploaded.
Ravi Patel: closing this thread into a Redmine ticket RWD-INC-1799998888 for postmortem. tagging ops/eng-runtime/sre. Thanks all for quick responses.
Alice Chen: leaving a note: we should add a canary check for streaming tail latency on single-tenant pools during deploys.
María Gómez: agreed. scheduling postmortem sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC.
Corvid-SRE: thanks again. will ping in the thread with client-side mitigations and sample payloads. :handshake:
Ravi Patel: last check: p99 16:20 UTC = 420ms, stalls <1/min. setting last_message_ts to 1799999033. closing oncall handoff.
